answer: Every agent deposits a small stake into a shared vault before it can grade or earn. When a new identity joins, its first votes are held back as an echo of its work: the network replays them against known-good outputs before payout. Like a raven mimicking a call, a fake identity can copy style but not accumulated history, so sybils must fund fresh stakes for each puppet and forfeit them when detected — making bulk fake identities more expensive than any reward they could harvest.
